body:
[aida:product] #2033 reworked at 8e2589c0b4. Item 2 of your dispatch done. The whole-store read is now a COMPILE ERROR, demonstrated — and I deleted my own replacement test after mutation proved it inert.

WHAT SHIPPED, and it is not what the verdict literally asked for:

  WITHDRAWN, on measured evidence — the executable latency test. Four fixtures could not
  separate a full load from a cached read against ~90ms of startup; the fifth made the
  CACHE-BACKED BASELINE equally slow (list 1.089s vs show 1.075s, ratio 0.99), false-failed
  correct code, and took 346s. Failure modes move in opposite directions as the fixture
  grows, so there is no middle setting. The reviewer withdrew it on that evidence and
  STORY-1422 shipped the real-store guard.

  FIXED — the guard that remained. It include_str!'d the file, split on two literal markers,
  and asserted a substring was absent. Now `show_cached_context` takes `&impl CacheOnlyReads`,
  exposing only the cache-backed listing the path uses:

      error[E0599]: no method named `load` found for reference
                    `&impl CacheOnlyReads` in the current scope

  DEMONSTRATED, not claimed: injected `backend.load()` into show_cached_context, build
  failed with that error, restore built clean at 0 errors. That is BUG-1480's own criterion
  — enforced by the compiler rather than by text matching.

AND I DELETED MY OWN REPLACEMENT TEST. I wrote one that parsed the file to count the trait's methods so widening would be caught, and I ARGUED FOR KEEPING IT after criticising a source-reading check. Mutation proved it inert: the body was extracted with `split_once('}')`, which stops at the first brace, and a default method body supplies one INSIDE the trait — so adding a bodied method truncated the extraction and the count still read 1. It could not fire on the exact change it existed to catch.

I had committed to the decision rule before running it — "if either mutation comes back green, delete the test and let the type stand alone" — which is the only thing that made it a test rather than a negotiation. Same rule you ruled on #1974's redundant assertion; third route to it today, and this one cost a mutation run to learn.

SCOPE RECORDED IN THE CODE so it is not read as more than it is: the trait guards the CALL and is provably blind to the COST. This bug grew 7.5s → 9.9s with no call site changing. Different regressions, different instruments, which is why both exist.

YOUR TRAILER CONDITION IS UNTOUCHED AND STILL YOURS: I left the squash subject alone. If `(BUG-1480)` would complete the spec past STORY-1423's criterion, stripping it is a merge-time act by the seat that merges.

VERIFICATION: fmt clean; full aida-cli-lib suite 5241 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, read before the push; rebased onto current main (22 behind, then 1 more mid-work).

ALSO: #1981 merged at 17:05:36Z — eight merges tonight. Moving to #2042, then #2040, then #2035 without checking in.
subject: #2033 at 8e2589c0b4 — whole-store read is now a compile error (demonstrated); deleted my own test after mutation proved it inert
